Hajdusamson Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Hajdúsámson, Hungary

Not demolished. One of two Jewish cemeteries in Hajdúsámson, established by 1805 and active until at least 1883. It holds the grave of Rabbi Jeremiás Mattersdorf, who served as Av Beit Din (head of a rabbinical court) in several communities. Jews first settled in Hajdúsámson in the early 18th century, trading at the local market; population reached 418 before steadily declining through the century, falling to 216 by 1941. Men were conscripted for forced labor from 1940, with some sent to the Ukrainian front in 1941. In April 1944, residents were confined to a farm camp near Debrecen under near-starvation conditions before transfer to a brick factory; most were then sent to Auschwitz, though a smaller group survived forced labor in Austria and later Theresienstadt. Thirty survivors briefly attempted to rebuild the community after the war before all left.
